name: Typeform
oneLiner: General-purpose form and survey builder known for its one-question-at-a-time conversational format, now with AI tools for building forms and analyzing answers.
bestFor: Smaller restaurant groups and marketing teams that want polished, branded feedback, catering-inquiry or event forms live quickly, and do not need POS integration, location benchmarking or closed-loop alerts.

updates.text: Winter 2025 release added an AI suite: an AI form builder that drafts questions from a prompt, plus AI sentiment analysis and insight summaries on responses.

Launched an AI engagement platform at Typeforum 2025, including Typeform AI (beta) that builds forms and follow-up workflows from a chat prompt, and AI that answers respondents' questions or asks clarifying follow-ups inside a form.

features: Conditional logic and branching based on earlier answers
Large template library, including restaurant and hotel feedback templates
AI form builder that drafts a survey from a prompt
AI sentiment analysis and summaries of open-text responses
Share by link, email, website embed or QR code
Branding controls (logo removal from the Plus plan up)
Integrations with HubSpot, Salesforce, Slack, Google Sheets, Mailchimp and Zapier

pricing.text: Free plan (10 responses/month). Paid plans per month billed yearly: Basic $28 (100 responses/month), Plus $56 (1,000), Business $91 (10,000); billed monthly $39 / $79 / $129. Enterprise is quoted.

notes: Pricing page could not be fetched directly; figures come from search snippets of typeform.com/pricing and typeform.com/ai-info, which agree. Third-party trackers report these prices took effect in 2026 (previously around $25/$50/$83 yearly) and mention extra tiers (Talent, Growth) not confirmed here; re-check before publishing. Dropped from current review: '$50+ for 1,000 responses on mid' tier wording (replace with the current figures above). 'Barcelona-based, founded in 2012' is commonly reported but was not re-checked in this research. No restaurant or hospitality customer story was found on Typeform's site; listed customers are Typeform's own case studies outside hospitality. Typeform remains a general-purpose tool, so it fits restaurants only as a lightweight survey option.
